name: Soybean
desc: A common Kharif pulse-oilseed option in suitable regions.
risks: Sensitive to waterlogging; verify local variety and sowing timing.
tip: Check local sowing recommendations with your district agriculture office.

tasks: Prepare a fine seedbed with good drainage.
Use certified seed of a locally recommended variety; treat seed with Rhizobium culture.
Sow at recommended spacing once soil moisture is adequate.
Check germination and fill gaps within the first fortnight.
Protect seedlings from heavy rain crusting; drain excess water quickly.
One hand weeding around 20–25 days (or as per local advice).
Keep the field free of the first flush of weeds.
Avoid moisture stress during flowering; irrigate only if the crop is rain-fed and dry.
Do not disturb the crop; support with locally approved plant-protection only if pests cross threshold.
Monitor for defoliator and girdle beetle activity as per local advisories.
Ensure drainage; soybean suffers badly in waterlogging.
Harvest when pods dry and leaves drop.
Dry and thresh promptly to avoid shattering losses.

name: Pearl millet (Bajra)
desc: A hardy grain crop option in suitable warm regions.
risks: Yield depends on rainfall timing and variety.
tip: Prioritize locally recommended drought-tolerant varieties.

tasks: Sow with the first effective monsoon showers on a fine seedbed.
Use certified seed of a drought-tolerant local variety.
Thin to one healthy plant per hill and fill gaps within two weeks.
Complete inter-cultivation and hand weeding.
Apply nitrogen top dressing only as per soil-test-based local advice.
Protect from moisture stress at boot stage if rain fails.
Watch for ergot/downy mildew symptoms; consult local advisory before any spray.
Protect ripening ears from birds.
Avoid excess moisture; drain waterlogged patches.
Harvest earheads when grains are hard; dry before threshing.
Store fodder for livestock use.

name: Sorghum (Jowar)
desc: A versatile grain and fodder crop used in rain-fed farming systems.
risks: Season and variety selection differ by region.
tip: Check region-specific guidance and soil moisture.

tasks: Sow on a prepared seedbed with adequate moisture.
Keep recommended row spacing for inter-cultivation.
Thin and gap-fill within two to three weeks of emergence.
Apply split nitrogen doses only as per local soil-test advice.
Complete weeding before the crop closes canopy.
Watch for shoot fly and stem borer; follow local integrated-pest advice.
Irrigate if available during long dry spells.
Protect from birds; drain excess water in Kharif.
Harvest grain at physiological maturity; cut fodder at the right stage.
Plan fodder storage or marketing along with grain.

name: Groundnut
desc: Can suit well-drained soils with a suitable rainfall pattern.
risks: Poor drainage can affect performance.
tip: Confirm drainage and local disease advice.

tasks: Sow well-filled kernels of a local recommended variety on a loose seedbed.
Ensure the field drains quickly; avoid low patches.
Complete first weeding before pegging begins.
Keep soil loose around plants so pegs can enter; apply gypsum only as per local advice.
Do not disturb the soil once pegging starts.
Maintain even moisture; avoid alternate wet-dry cycles.
Monitor for leaf miner and tikka disease per local advisories.
Scratch-test pods: dark inside-shell markings indicate maturity.
Lift, shake off soil and dry pods in shade first, then sun.
Store dry pods below 8–9% moisture to avoid aflatoxin risk.

name: Maize
desc: A multi-season crop where water and local markets are suitable.
risks: Water needs rise at flowering and grain filling.
tip: Check local water availability and buyer access.

tasks: Sow certified seed at recommended spacing and depth.
Plan market/buyer link before choosing grain vs. green-cob vs. fodder type.
Thin to one plant per hill; fill gaps within 10 days.
Apply first nitrogen top dressing as per local soil-test advice.
Earthing-up after top dressing helps stand the crop.
Maize needs the most water from knee-high to grain filling; irrigate if dry.
Scout weekly for fall armyworm; follow local IPM guidance.
Maintain moisture; avoid stress which cuts grain size.
Harvest when husk dries and grains show black layer.
Dry cobs to safe moisture before shelling and storage.

name: Rice (Paddy)
desc: A crop for suitable lowland or irrigated conditions.
risks: Usually a higher-water option.
tip: Use a locally recommended variety.

tasks: Raise nursery with certified seed of a locally recommended variety.
Transplant 20–25 day seedlings at recommended spacing in puddled field.
Maintain thin standing water after transplanting.
Apply nitrogen in splits as per local advice; complete weeding.
Keep water 2–5 cm deep; do not let the field crack.
Apply final nitrogen top dressing per local recommendation.
Watch for stem borer and leaf folder; follow local advisories.
Never let the crop stress at flowering; keep shallow water.
Avoid pesticide sprays during peak flowering hours to protect bees.
Drain the field gradually near maturity as per local practice.
Harvest at 20–25% grain moisture; dry to 14% before storage.
Plan straw management; avoid burning where restricted.

name: Cotton
desc: A region-specific cash crop associated with suitable soils and a long season.
risks: Long duration, pests and input costs create risk.
tip: Review local pest-management and seed guidance.

tasks: Sow certified seed after soil warms and monsoon settles.
Use recommended spacing; deep black soils suit this deep-rooted crop.
Thin to recommended plant population; fill gaps early.
Apply balanced nutrition per soil-test advice; avoid excess nitrogen.
Install traps/pheromone lures as per local pest-management guidance.
Scout twice weekly for pink bollworm and sucking pests; act only on thresholds.
Avoid unnecessary broad-spectrum sprays; protect natural enemies.
Pick clean, dry kapas in 2–3 rounds; keep grades separate.
Moist kapas spoils quality — never pick wet bolls.
Remove and destroy stalks to break pest cycles before next season.
Plan soil test after long-duration crop.

name: Chickpea (Chana)
desc: A Rabi pulse option with suitable residual moisture.
risks: Excess moisture and disease pressure may affect the crop.
tip: Check soil moisture and local disease precautions.

tasks: Sow on residual moisture with a locally recommended variety.
Seed treatment per local advice; avoid sowing too deep.
Nipping (top clipping) as practiced locally may improve branching.
Keep field weed-free; one hand weeding around 25–30 days.
Scout for pod borer (Helicoverpa) weekly; use local IPM advice — pheromone traps, bird perches.
One light irrigation at flowering/branching if available.
Avoid excess water; chickpea fails more often from moisture than drought.
Harvest when pods dry and plants turn straw-coloured.
Dry to safe moisture before threshing and storage.

name: Wheat
desc: Can suit Rabi conditions where temperature, soil and irrigation match.
risks: Heat during grain filling and limited irrigation affect yields.
tip: Verify regional suitability and sowing date.

tasks: Sow a locally recommended variety in the correct window; late sowing costs yield.
Use seed rate per local advice; place fertilizer as recommended.
First irrigation around 20–25 days is the most critical one.
Apply first nitrogen top dressing before or with this irrigation.
Second irrigation; keep weeds in check (weed-free first 40 days matter most).
Third irrigation; watch for yellow rust alerts in your district.
Never skip irrigation at booting.
Protect from terminal heat; evening irrigation can help if heat wave is forecast.
Monitor for rust and aphid as per local advisories.
Harvest when grain is hard and straw golden; combine or manual as available.
Dry grain to 12% moisture for storage.

name: Mustard
desc: An oilseed option in selected Rabi regions.
risks: Regional adaptation varies.
tip: Check whether mustard is recommended in your district.

tasks: Sow in the recommended Rabi window with proper seed rate.
Keep rows spaced for inter-cultivation.
Thin to keep healthy plants; remove excess seedlings.
First irrigation at rosette stage (~30 days) with nitrogen top dressing as per advice.
Watch aphid clusters on shoots; use local IPM thresholds before spraying.
Protect bees — mustard depends on pollination.
Second irrigation at siliqua filling if needed; avoid over-watering.
Harvest when 75% siliquae turn yellow-brown; avoid shattering.
Dry and thresh; store oilseed in dry conditions.

name: Onion
desc: A higher-management horticulture option where drainage and markets suit.
risks: Price swings, storage and disease can substantially affect returns.
tip: Check local prices, storage and crop-protection costs.

tasks: Transplant 6–8 week nursery seedlings on raised beds with good drainage.
Plan storage and market link before committing area — onion is price-volatile.
Light, frequent irrigation; onion roots are shallow.
Top dressing per soil-test advice; keep beds weed-free.
Maintain even moisture; stress now splits or doubles bulbs.
Monitor thrips weekly; follow local plant-protection advice.
Continue light irrigation; do not overwater near maturity.
Purple blotch/alternaria watch — act per local advisory only.
Stop irrigation when 50–70% tops fall over.
Lift, cure bulbs in shade with tops for 2–3 weeks where suitable.
Sort and grade before storage or sale; diseased bulbs must be removed.

name: Green gram (Moong)
desc: A relatively short-duration pulse for locally suitable windows.
risks: Sensitive to sowing window, pests and rainfall distribution.
tip: Confirm local variety, timing and demand.

tasks: Sow a locally recommended short-duration variety; precise window matters.
One weeding around 20 days keeps the fast crop clean.
Avoid moisture stress at flowering if irrigating; rain-fed crops depend on timely showers.
Watch whitefly/jassids and pod borers; follow local IPM advice.
Avoid sprays close to harvest.
Pick mature pods in 1–2 rounds; dry and thresh promptly.
Short duration frees the field for the next crop — plan rotation.

name: Sugarcane
desc: A long-duration crop grown in suitable irrigated districts with access to a mill.
risks: High water, capital and market-access requirements; not suitable for every farm.
tip: Verify water allocation, planting window and mill access locally.

tasks: Plant healthy setts of an approved variety in the district planting window.
Ensure assured irrigation and a mill/gur market link BEFORE planting.
Fill gaps and complete first top dressing per local advice.
Begin inter-cultivation and earthing-up as canes grow.
Peak water demand — schedule irrigation strictly per local guidance.
Split nitrogen applications as per soil-test-based advice.
Continue irrigation; propping/tying prevents lodging in wind.
Monitor for borers and wilt per local advisories.
Reduce irrigation near maturity as advised; sucrose accumulates best in dry, clear weather.
Harvest per mill slip/calendar; strip and deliver promptly — delays cut weight and quality.
Plan ratoon management or rotation after harvest.

name: Quinoa
desc: Andean protein-rich pseudocereal being evaluated in Odisha, Gujarat, Rajasthan and Maharashtra. A diversification option, not yet a mainstream crop.
risks: Sensitive to heat at flowering and to waterlogging; saline soils and a thin buyer market are real risks. Verify variety, sowing window and a buyer first.
tip: Start with a small trial plot and a confirmed buyer; check variety and sowing window with your KVK.

tasks: Prepare a fine, well-drained seedbed; quinoa seed is very small, so avoid deep sowing.
Use seed of a locally trialled variety and sow in the cool-season window advised by your KVK.
Thin seedlings to the recommended spacing for good branching.
Give a light irrigation only if the seedbed dries out.
Weed by hand or inter-cultivation in the early weeks; the crop is a weak competitor when young.
Irrigate sparingly as per local advice; avoid waterlogging.
Scout for aphids and leaf-feeding insects and follow district plant-protection advice.
Avoid moisture stress and very hot spells at flowering; watch the weather forecast.
Protect the crop from birds at grain filling.
Harvest when leaves have dropped and seed is hard; avoid harvesting in rain.
Dry and thresh promptly; saponin-removal (washing/polishing) is needed before sale.

name: Chia
desc: Mexican seed crop (fibre and omega-3) with ICAR practices for drought-prone areas; worth investigating in Maharashtra, Karnataka and Telangana.
risks: Very photoperiod-sensitive, so the sowing window matters a lot; seed source and buyer demand must be confirmed before planting.
tip: Look up the latest ICAR chia cultivation practices and confirm the sowing window locally.

tasks: Prepare a fine seedbed; chia seed is tiny and must be sown shallow.
Sow in the window recommended locally using seed from a reliable source.
Check emergence and thin to the recommended spacing.
Keep the field weed-free during the first 4-5 weeks.
Irrigate lightly only if the crop is stressed; chia is drought tolerant once established.
Scout for sucking pests and follow district advisories.
Avoid water stress at flowering; avoid waterlogging.
Harvest when most flower spikes have dried and seed is mature.
Dry, thresh and clean the seed; store at low moisture.

name: Grain amaranth (Rajgira)
desc: Nutritious grain also grown in India (hill regions and other adapted areas); a hardy option for crop diversification.
risks: Small seed needs careful sowing; shattering at harvest and limited local buyers can reduce returns.
tip: Choose a locally adapted variety and check the market for amaranth grain before sowing.

tasks: Prepare a fine seedbed; mix the tiny seed with sand or soil for even sowing.
Thin seedlings to recommended spacing for large seed heads.
Hand-weed in the first month; the crop competes well afterwards.
Irrigate only when needed; amaranth tolerates dry spells.
Avoid moisture stress at flowering; watch for caterpillars and follow local advice.
Harvest when heads turn dry and seed is hard; cut early morning to reduce shattering.
Dry heads on a clean floor, then thresh and winnow.

name: Buckwheat (Kuttu)
desc: Gluten-free short-season crop used in Himalayan and north-eastern hill systems (Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Sikkim).
risks: Sensitive to heat and frost and to moisture stress at flowering; best suited to cool hill climates.
tip: Mainly for hill areas; confirm altitude, frost window and sowing time with local hill agriculture offices.

tasks: Prepare a fine, well-drained seedbed.
Sow when frost risk has passed, using locally adapted seed.
Check emergence; buckwheat emerges quickly in cool moist soil.
One weeding in the first 3 weeks; the crop then shades weeds out.
Avoid moisture stress; flowers depend on insect pollination, so keep bees in mind when using plant protection.
Watch for frost and heavy rain; seed matures unevenly.
Harvest when most seed is dark; cut early to limit shattering.
Dry the cut plants a few days before threshing.

name: Moringa (Drumstick)
desc: Indian-origin tree with edible pods and leaves; drought tolerant once established and grown across Maharashtra, Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh and Telangana.
risks: Waterlogging kills young plants; pod prices swing with seasonal gluts; leaf/powder markets need a confirmed buyer.
tip: Pick a recommended pod or leaf variety and plan pruning to keep branches at harvestable height.

tasks: Dig pits or ridges with good drainage; mix in farmyard manure.
Plant healthy seedlings or direct-sow seed at recommended spacing at the start of the rains.
Water young plants carefully; never let water stand around the stem.
Protect saplings from grazing and strong wind.
Pinch the growing tip at the recommended height to encourage side branches.
Avoid heavy irrigation at flowering; scout for pod fly and leaf-eating caterpillars per local advice.
Pick tender pods at the right stage; grade and sell quickly, as pods are perishable.
Plan annual pruning after the main harvest.

name: Dragon fruit
desc: Cactus fruit grown widely in Asia with experience in parts of Maharashtra, Gujarat, Karnataka and southern India; a high-investment specialty fruit.
risks: High support-structure cost, sunburn and heat risk, waterlogging and 1-1.5 years before fruit. Confirm buyers before investing.
tip: Visit a working dragon-fruit farm and read ICAR sunburn-management guidance before investing.

tasks: Prepare well-drained land and install concrete or sturdy poles with top support.
Plant healthy, callused cuttings at the base of each pole.
Tie shoots to the pole and train them upward; remove side shoots until the top is reached.
Irrigate lightly (drip is ideal) and keep the base weed-free.
Allow branches to hang from the pole top; apply manure per soil-test advice.
Shade or whitewash exposed stems in peak summer to reduce sunburn.
Flowering happens in summer-monsoon flushes; avoid water stress.
Scout for fungal rots and ants/insects per local advice.
Harvest when the skin is fully coloured; handle gently.
Sort, grade and sell to confirmed buyers or processors.

name: Avocado
desc: Mexican-origin fruit tree with specialty-market potential in selected climates of southern India, Maharashtra and the Northeast.
risks: Highly sensitive to waterlogging and root rot; 3-5 years to meaningful yield; needs selected mild, humid climates.
tip: Only consider if your district is known for avocado, and use grafted plants from a reliable nursery.

tasks: Choose well-drained land; avoid any waterlogged spot.
Dig pits and fill with soil mixed with farmyard manure.
Plant grafted saplings from a reliable nursery at the start of the rains; stake them.
Water young trees carefully; mulch to hold moisture.
Protect from strong wind and frost.
Prune lightly to shape the tree and remove weak branches.
Avoid water stress at flowering; scout for root rot and follow local advice.
Mature fruit ripens off the tree; harvest by clipping with the stalk.
Plan cold-chain or quick sale, as ripe fruit is perishable.

name: Passion fruit
desc: Tropical American vine for fresh use, juice and processing; relevant for the Northeast and parts of Karnataka, Kerala and Tamil Nadu.
risks: Needs a trellis, is prone to virus and wilt diseases, and needs a processor or reliable fresh-fruit market.
tip: Link with a processor or pulp buyer before planting; use disease-free planting material.

tasks: Set up a sturdy trellis or pergola and prepare drained planting pits.
Plant disease-free seedlings or cuttings at the start of the rains.
Train the main shoot up the trellis; pinch to encourage laterals.
Irrigate regularly but avoid waterlogging.
Prune and feed as per local recommendations.
Scout for virus symptoms and wilt; remove diseased vines.
Flowers depend on pollinators; avoid water stress.
Pick fruit as it drops or turns colour; grade for fresh market or processing.

name: Blueberry
desc: High-value North American berry. In India it suits only cool sites or carefully managed growing systems with acidic, well-drained soil.
risks: Needs acidic soil (low pH), cool climate and heavy investment; most farms are not suitable. Do not invest without expert trials.
tip: Treat as an experimental crop; consult ICAR/KVK or an experienced grower before any investment.

tasks: Test soil pH; blueberries need strongly acidic, well-drained soil.
Prepare raised beds enriched with acidic organic matter.
Plant certified saplings in the cool season.
Mulch heavily and irrigate regularly with low-salt water.
Remove flower buds in the first year to build the plant.
Prune out weak or old wood; feed with acid-forming fertilisers as per soil test.
Protect flowers from frost; ensure pollinators are present.
Hand-pick ripe berries several times; chill quickly after picking.

name: Cape gooseberry (Rasbhari)
desc: South American berry for fresh fruit and processing; worth investigating in Maharashtra, Karnataka and hill states.
risks: Sensitive to frost and waterlogging; fruit is perishable and the market is thin in many districts.
tip: Start on a small area; avoid fields that grew tomato, brinjal or potato last season.

tasks: Raise seedlings in a nursery or tray; harden before transplanting.
Transplant healthy seedlings at recommended spacing on well-drained land.
Irrigate lightly; stake plants where needed.
Weed and apply nutrients per soil test advice.
Scout for borers and wilt per local advice.
Avoid water stress; mulch to hold moisture.
Pick when the husk turns dry and golden; harvest every few days.
Sell fresh or to processors; fruit keeps best in its husk.

name: Stevia
desc: South American leaf crop used as a sweetener; viable only with suitable climate and a confirmed buyer or processor.
risks: Buy-back is essential: without a processor contract the dried-leaf market is unreliable. Sensitive to waterlogging and extreme cold/heat.
tip: Do not plant without a written buy-back agreement from a stevia processor.

tasks: Prepare raised, well-drained beds enriched with compost.
Transplant healthy rooted cuttings at recommended spacing.
Irrigate lightly and often; keep beds weed-free.
Pinch the tips to encourage branching; apply nutrients per soil test.
Harvest leaves just before flowering, when sweetness is highest.
Cut the plant at recommended height and dry leaves in shade or a dryer.
Deliver dried leaf to the confirmed buyer; allow regrowth for the next cutting.

name: Saffron (Kesar)
desc: High-value spice from Kashmir and other traditional zones. Anywhere else, only validated trials are advisable.
risks: Very specific climate and soil needs, very high corm cost and labour-intensive picking; outside traditional zones results are uncertain.
tip: Outside Kashmir, only try saffron as a small, expert-guided trial.

tasks: Prepare raised, well-drained beds; saffron corms rot in wet soil.
Plant healthy, disease-free corms at recommended depth and spacing in the correct season.
Keep soil lightly moist; never allow waterlogging.
Flowers open for a short period; pick early morning each day.
Separate the red stigmas by hand and dry them carefully.
Let the leaves grow so corms multiply for the next season.
Weed the bed and avoid disturbing the corms; plan the next cycle.

name: Lavender
desc: Mediterranean essential-oil and fragrance crop, grown in selected Himalayan areas and suitable specialised sites.
risks: Needs a cool climate and very well-drained soil; oil yields depend on distillation access and a buyer.
tip: Confirm distillation access and an oil buyer before planting more than a trial plot.

tasks: Prepare well-drained, light soil; lavender hates standing water.
Plant rooted cuttings at recommended spacing in the correct season.
Keep weed-free; irrigate lightly until established.
Prune lightly after the first season to shape bushes.
Harvest flower spikes at the right bloom stage for oil.
Distill promptly after cutting; sell oil to the confirmed buyer.

name: Rosemary
desc: Mediterranean culinary herb and essential-oil plant, suitable for well-drained sites in parts of western and southern India.
risks: Dislikes wet soil and heavy rain; price depends on a nearby herb, spice or oil buyer.
tip: Plant on well-drained soil and find a buyer (spice units, restaurants or oil makers) first.

tasks: Prepare well-drained, light soil with some compost.
Plant rooted cuttings at recommended spacing.
Irrigate lightly; avoid wet feet and keep beds weed-free.
Pinch tips to encourage bushy growth.
Cut healthy shoots (about a third of the plant) for fresh or dried sale.
Allow regrowth between cuttings.
Dry in shade, pack, and sell to confirmed buyers.

name: Shiitake mushroom
desc: East-Asian specialty mushroom grown indoors on substrate; not land-based, so it suits farms with space, facilities and temperature control.
risks: Cost shown is a small fruiting-room setup, not per acre. Needs temperature and humidity control, clean substrate handling and a perishable-food market.
tip: Take a short mushroom-growing course (KVK or ICAR training) and sell through local buyers before scaling.

tasks: Prepare a clean room with shade, ventilation and humidity control.
Prepare and sterilise the substrate (sawdust or agricultural residue) as trained.
Inoculate bags with quality shiitake spawn in a clean area.
Keep bags in the dark at the recommended temperature; watch for green mould.
Move bags to the fruiting area; maintain humidity and fresh air.
Pick mushrooms when the cap is open, then grade and chill them.
Sell fresh or dried to confirmed buyers; refer to a safe handling guide.
